chapter_theme: The sixth part of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi finishes the attack on the alchemists who live by trickery (fumes blown through a tube, calx sold to the credulous, flying mercury and magnet cups) and on ganja-smoking cave ascetics, then turns the alchemist's words inward: the salt, the root, the black gooseberry and the white root in the tank are in the house, and the true alchemist is the one who knows the salt. After naming the Siddha books it trusts (Konkanar, Sattamuni, Tirumular, Agastya, Machamuni), it lists as mere desire every outward observance, the breath-counting of rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka included, along with giving up salt, eating once a day, pilgrimage, the family god, sect difference and Ganga bathing, and ends by turning from the six adharas to the Vedantic count of tattvas.
structure_note: False alchemists and false gurus (2643 to 2647); alchemy read as an inner work, its salt, root and herbs coded as in the body (2648 to 2652); ganja ascetics, and the books of the true Siddhas (2653 to 2656); the litany of what is only desire (ஆசையடி), with the gate within the gate set among it (2657 to 2661); casting off Pati and pasa, the tattvas, the Veda and the six adharas (2662 to 2664); the turn to Vedanta and the count of tattvas, which the next part sets out (2665 to 2667). The refrains ஞானப்பெண்ணே and கும்மியடியுங்கடி alternate; the readings give what each stanza adds.

2643.reading: They do not see the key of alchemy, nor perceive the drug of the five elements; why do they blow smoke through the tube? Ask what this is, girl of knowledge.
2643.nuance: The திறவுகோல் (key) of vaadham is what the kummi will say is inward; பஞ்சபூதச் சரக்கு, the drug of the five elements, can be read as an actual mineral set or as the five elements of the body. குழல் புகை ஊதுதல், blowing fumes through the blowpipe, is the outward craft being mocked.

2644.reading: They say the sacred calx is finished and the test-piece has been changed, tell of the substance and carry off money: are these not false gurus, girl of knowledge?
2644.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are compressed and partly corrupt (சுன்னம் is calx; வெட்டாரை is unclear, perhaps a test or a vessel). Line 3 is plain: the alchemist-guru describes the marvel and takes fees. The charge is fraud, not the falsity of alchemy as such.

2645.reading: They say the flying mercury is done, they say they have made even the needle-magnet into a cup; it is by the trickery of their world-alchemy that they make a living, girl of knowledge.
2645.nuance: கவன சூதம், mercury fixed so that it gives the power to fly (கமனம்), and the magnet worked into a vessel are boasts of the alchemical literature. புவனவாதை may be புவன வாதம், alchemy for the world's eyes, against the inner alchemy the kummi prefers.

2646.reading: Living on without knowing release or the knowledge brought from former births, they feed on rain, wither to dry leaves and falter, girl of knowledge.
2646.nuance: மழையைத் தின்று, 'eating the rain', is read as the ascetic who lives on water or air and wastes to a dry leaf (சருகு); the line may be corrupt. The point is that bodily austerity without knowledge is only a slower way of failing.

2647.reading: What fruit is there in faltering? Is it skill to master the mind and then sell it? Do not be deluded: how does the greatness of the vazhalai come?
2647.nuance: வழலை is the Siddhars' alchemical salt (in some lists the base of muppu), and in their cipher a thing of the body. The question 'how does its greatness come?' prepares the next stanza's answer that the salt is known, not bought. மனம் சாதித்து விற்க may mean making a trade of mental powers.

2648.reading: He who knows the salt is the alchemist, he who has destroyed the world's dross is the yogi; there is no fault in this; lean on the glory of earth and nada and see, girl of knowledge.
2648.nuance: The stanza redefines both titles: வாதி is not the one with the crucible but the one who knows உப்பு, the salt that in Siddha cipher stands for a bodily essence, and யோகி is the one rid of the world's குப்பை, its rubbish. பூமி நாத மகிமை, 'the glory of earth and nada', is obscure; it may pair the base centre with the sound at the crown.

2649.reading: There is a root in the house, and in the forest outside is Tirumular; for the great ones who are caught in it, is this not rasavada, girl of knowledge?
2649.nuance: The stanza puns on மூலம்: the herb-root sought in the forest, the மூலாதாரம் at the base of the body that is 'in the house', and திருமூலர், the Siddha whose name is the 'holy root'. The plain sense is that the root for alchemy is at home; the coded sense is that the true rasavada is the root centre, as Tirumular taught.

2650.reading: Taking the drug they say does not appear, setting it in the black ... and drawing it out: like the thing seen by one who cannot see, siddhi is that itself; dance the kummi.
2650.nuance: கருஞ்சூரசூரை is corrupt or a coded vessel name and is not rendered. காணான் கண்ட பொருள், 'the thing the blind man saw', is a Siddha paradox for what is seen without the eye; the attainment is the seeing, not the product.

2651.reading: The gooseberry is in the forest and the black gooseberry is in the house; even if you go off to the Kolli hills, will the guru bring it to you, girl of knowledge?
2651.nuance: கருநெல்லி, the black gooseberry, is a famous kalpa herb of the Siddha tradition, said to grow on the Kolli hills; the stanza moves it 'into the house', the body. The question about the guru can be read as scorn (no guru will fetch it for you) or as a pointer (only the guru shows where it is).

2652.reading: In the tank of Kayampatti the white kasa root has sprouted; if one rises upright from the mouth-river, the body will not perish, girl of knowledge.
2652.nuance: காயாம்பட்டி reads as the 'village of the body' (காயம்), its tank a bodily place; காசாம் வேர், the root of the kasa (white-flowered) plant, is a herb or its cipher. வாயாற்றினின்று நிமிர்ந்தால், rising from the river of the mouth, may point to the turning of breath or nectar upward. The claim is the kalpa claim of an undying body, here located within.

2653.reading: Without thinking to know the kalpa state they smoke maddening ganja and stay so; even if these petty men go to caves and mountains, can they know the thing, girl of knowledge?
2653.nuance: The target is the ascetic who uses ganja as a shortcut and the remote cave as a credential. கற்பநிலை, the kalpa state, is again inward.

2654.reading: In the Kadaikkandam that Konkanar told, knowing what is in doubt is the Brahmanda; see the two hundred of our guru, the great muni Sattaimuni, girl of knowledge.
2654.nuance: The stanza names Siddha books: Konkanar's கடைக்காண்டம் and Sattaimuni's இருநூறு (two hundred verses), and claims Sattaimuni as 'our guru'. The middle phrase, that knowing the doubt in it is பிரமாண்டம், may mean the book's secret is the cosmic egg, or simply that it is vast.

2655.reading: What the true jnani told in the hundred, what Tirumular realised, is jnana; see the locked secret of the sutra that Purna Kumbhamuni told, girl of knowledge.
2655.nuance: கும்பமுனி is Agastya; 'the hundred' is not identified. பூட்டகம், a locked thing, names the Siddha habit of writing so that only the initiated can open the text.

2656.reading: In initiation, Machamuni's initiation and the hundred of knowledge he declared: no lowering will come; see the great ones and hear the vision, girl of knowledge.
2656.nuance: மச்சமுனி (Matsyendra in the north) is cited for தீட்சை, initiation, and a work of a hundred verses. The stanza closes the list of authorities by sending the hearer to living great ones.

2657.reading: Doing the vaasi exactly by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka is also desire; reach the non-dual Brahman that is the sky-going state and dance the kummi.
2657.nuance: This opens the litany of ஆசையடி, 'that too is desire'. Breath-counting is placed among the observances to be outgrown, although the same kummi taught the vaasi at the root triangle (2593, 2615). One reading is that the measured pranayama of the manuals is the desire, and the vaasi proper is the khechara Brahman itself; another is that at this point the song leaves practice for Vedanta. கேசரம் is the 'moving in space' that 2642 promised the inner alchemy.

2658.reading: Giving up salt is desire, eating food only once a day is desire; join the Manonmani god who cannot be spoken and dance the kummi.
2658.nuance: The vows of abstaining from salt and of a single daily meal are reckoned with desire, as wanting a result. The salt here is literal, unlike the coded salt of 2648, so the kummi both praises knowing the salt and dismisses giving it up. மனோன்மணி is the Shakti of the crown, 'jewel of the mind'.

2659.reading: In the gate there is an upper gate, and in that gate a small gate; lovingly close the small gate and look closely, girl of knowledge.
2659.nuance: The first two lines repeat 2561 almost word for word. The gate within the gate is the Siddhars' cipher for the opening of the central channel at the crown; பூட்டி நெருக்கி, locking and pressing, is read as the inward seal of breath and mind. Set between two 'desire' stanzas, it marks what is not desire.

2660.reading: Going to far lands is desire, saying there is a family god is desire; join the light of the Brahman-knowledge we love and dance the kummi.
2660.nuance: தேசங்கள் போவது is pilgrimage or wandering; குலதெய்வம் is the lineage deity of the household. Both are put on the side of wanting.

2661.reading: Sect difference is desire, bathing in the Ganga and puja are desire; praise the 'mine' that remains without 'mine', and dance the kummi.
2661.nuance: மமதை அற்றிருக்கின்ற மமதை, 'the mineness that stays without mineness', is a paradox: perhaps the Self that alone can say 'I' without ego, perhaps a scribal doubling. The first half is the common Siddha rejection of sect and sacred water.

2662.reading: Push away the cow that gives no milk, leave even Pati and pasa and be done with them; seek the Supreme light that shines above and dance the kummi.
2662.nuance: பதி and பாசம் are two of Saiva Siddhanta's three categories (with பசு); telling the hearer to leave the Lord-category itself is a Vedantic move beyond the Siddhanta scheme. பால் கறவாப் பசு, the cow that yields no milk, may be the barren practice or, by pun on பசு, the bound soul's identity.

2663.reading: Push away the rubbish heap of the tattvas, close up the holes of Veda and sastra; call the knowledge-thing that gives release to come, kindle it and dance the kummi.
2663.nuance: பொத்தல் is a hole or gap (or a scribal form of பொத்தகம், book); either way the Veda and the sastras are to be shut. Two stanzas later the kummi takes up Vedanta 'by the word of the Siddhars', so the dismissal is of book-learning, not of the Vedantic conclusion.

2664.reading: The six adharas are trouble, and beyond them there is nothing; women standing in good order, join and dance the kummi.
2664.nuance: அதற்கு அப்பாலே ஒன்றுமில்லை, 'beyond it there is nothing', can mean that the climb through the six centres leads nowhere, or that beyond them is the void, the nothing the kummi elsewhere calls the goal (2698). Both readings stand.

2665.reading: By the Siddhars' word see Siddhanta and be clear about Vedanta; hear the relation of the subtle origin that is tattva, girl of knowledge.
2665.nuance: The kummi claims Siddhanta and Vedanta both, with the Siddhars as the authority for each, and announces the Vedantic account of how the tattvas arise, which the stanzas following set out.

2666.reading: What is the relation? The tattva that Vedanta tells is of this kind; I will lay out the account of the states, the causal and the rest, girl of knowledge.
2666.nuance: காரணாதி அவஸ்தை, the states beginning with the causal, announces the scheme of bodies and states (gross, subtle, causal; waking, dream, sleep) that the next part develops.

2667.reading: The tattvas spoken of are seen as four sevens, the chit-form told is four sixes; see the greatness of the chit-form spoken within the Veda, girl of knowledge.
2667.nuance: நாலேழு and நாலாறு are read as 28 and 24; the text could also mean eleven and ten. A count of twenty-eight tattvas is known from Tirumanthiram 2176; what the 'chit-form' of twenty-four is, the stanza does not say, and line 3 is corrupt (சித்துருதாலாகு).

links.note: Both describe the alchemist-guru who announces a transmutation and walks off with the client's money; Valaisami names such men false gurus, the other poem tracks them a league away. The Siddhars' quarrel with alchemists is first about fraud.
The Kural calls hardest of heart those who live by deceit while seeming to have renounced; Valaisami's false gurus, who talk of the substance and take money, are that type in an alchemist's dress.

Both make salt the alchemist's secret and place it within: the other verse says that of the many kinds of rock salt the true one is in the inner mind; Valaisami says the alchemist is simply the one who knows the salt.

The black gooseberry, the Siddha kalpa herb, appears in both: there as something to pluck and eat so the head will not burn, here as already growing in the house, so that no trip to the Kolli hills is needed. The second reads the first's herb as cipher.
Both attack the ascetic who smokes ganja and passes for an eater of kalpa; Valaisami adds that going to caves and mountains does not change what such men can know.

In the same kummi, 2593 makes kundalini's vaasi at the root triangle the knowing itself; 2657 counts doing the vaasi by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka as desire. On the reading that the vaasi is meant in both, the song first prescribes and then dismisses the practice; the conflict dissolves only if the measured pranayama of 2657 is distinguished from the vaasi of 2593.

Tirumular gives the measures of puraka, kumbhaka and rechaka (sixteen, sixty-four, thirty-two) and calls any change of the order deceit; Valaisami calls doing the vaasi by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka mere desire. One makes exact breath-counting the truth, the other an attachment to be left for the non-dual Brahman.

The gate in the gate, with its small gate, recurs almost verbatim from the temple section of the kummi; there one looks at the tight lock, here one closes the small gate oneself, and the image now stands among the observances rejected as desire, as the one that is not.
Tirumular says the holy waters are within the heart and those who do not bathe there wander over hill and hollow; Valaisami counts Ganga bathing and puja as desire. Both move the tirtha inward.
The other verse asks whether karma leaves at Kasi or with bathing in the Ganga; Valaisami answers the same question by naming the bathing as desire, and adds sect difference to the list.

Tirumular calls the Veda and the Agama the two the Lord spoke, which in due order become Vedanta and Siddhanta; Valaisami tells the girl to shut up the holes of Veda and sastra, yet two stanzas later takes up Vedanta and Siddhanta 'by the Siddhars' word'. He keeps the conclusion and drops the books Tirumular treats as its source.

If நாலேழு is read as twenty-eight, Valaisami's count of tattvas matches Tirumular's twenty-eight, twenty-three with prakriti plus turiya, time, the void and the higher turiya. The agreement rests on the numeral reading.

source_issues: 2644: lines 1 and 2 (திருசுசுன்னமுடிந்தாச்சு அசைச் சோதிக்க வெட்டாரை மாற்றாச்சு) are compressed or corrupt.
2649: மிதல்வவோ is a misprint for மிதல்லவோ.
2650: கருஞ்சூரசூரை is corrupt; வைத்தெடுப்பச் has a stray final letter.
2651: பெணணே is a misprint for பெண்ணே.
2652 and 2662: the stanzas end with a stray comma after the refrain.
2660: சே.தி has a stray full stop, for சோதி; கும்மி படியுங்கடி for கும்மியடியுங்கடி.
2665: சேளடி is a misprint for கேளடி.
